newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end up on Dec options expiry.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end up on Dec options expiry.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly higher on Friday, as the complex continued to recover, with help from the December gold and silver options expiry, from a slump seen early this week.

"December gold closed above $380 which was surprising as it opened lower, but there was some spreading and rolling of positions around the December options expiry which may explain it," Friedberg Mercantile Group's Toronto trader Jeff Kowal said. "I still think it could lower."
COMEX December gold closed up 90 cents at $380.50, after again finding support around $378 early in the day.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $379.20/379.70 an ounce, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $378.15, and the New York close Thursday at $378.75/379.25.
A fall in open interest in December gold futures this week and a narrowing of the contangos reflected the rolling of positions into forward months, analysts said.

Open interest in December gold futures fell 6,682 lots Thursday and total gold open interest was down 4,263 lots, while the December/April gold spread narrowed further to $3.89 an ounce Friday also, its lowest level since February.

After spot gold saw a 19 month low at $376.80 last week, prices have consolidated this week, but popular trend following indicators, such as the four, nine and 18 day moving-averages, remain in downtrends.
"Proprietary traders still seem to be gunning for the $374 downside target, with an eye on longer term support at $370," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
COMEX December silver ended up 0.5 cent at $4.838 an ounce, after recovering from a morning low at $4.765.
The partial recovery in silver followed a slide in spot silver in the bullion market to 18 month lows at $4.72 Wednesday.
NYMEX January platinum ended up 70 cents at $387.00, after seeing a fresh life-of-contract low at $382.00 Wednesday, while NYMEX December palladium closed down five cents at $118.00.

Platinum group metals prices have also been struggling to find a base, after spot platinum saw 35 month lows at $378.25 an ounce last Friday, while palladium saw 43 month lows at $114.00 last Thursday, analysts said.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
